scenario: AITA for not staying home and taking care of my sick wife all weekend? | On Thursday evening my wife started feeling unwell. I encouraged her to go to bed and told her I could handle the kids evening stuff by myself (3 kids, ages 9, 11, and 13). I checked on her after the kids were in bed at 9 and she was fevered- I asked if she wanted any medicine, made sure she had some water, and rubbed her back for a few minutes. I slept in the spare room but got up twice to check on her. The next morning I got the kids ready and off to school, went to a meeting and came home at 10 to take her to the doctor. I worked from home until our cleaning lady came around 1 and asked her to keep an eye on my wife and went back into the office for a couple meetings, picked up the kids and was home around 4. Her fever broke shortly after I got home at 4 and I helped her shower. Our oldest had a school dance and I got some movies and set the youngest 2 up in the den for the evening with pizza and some games so they'd be quiet. I checked on my wife periodically and after the oldest got home me and the 3 kids camped out in the den. On Saturday morning, the kids were restless so I took them out for the day bc I didn't want them to be around the house being loud. I checked on my wife and she was sleeping- I refilled her water and left her a note. Throughout the day I called and sent her messages and my mom took her over some homemade soup and checked on her. We were gone the majority of the day but the kids came home worn out and we crashed in the den again. I checked on my wife as soon as we got home and she was looking better. Sunday morning, the kids and I woke up early, did some yardwork then went to the store to do the weekly grocery shopping. When we got home my wife was up and about and still weak but feeling better. However, she was being really short with me and was in a bad mood. I thought it was just bc she didn't feel well but after a few hours of her making snide comments I asked her if something was wrong and she exploded on me that her family abandoned her while she was sick. She went off about how she always takes care of us when we're sick but we avoided her like the plague and didn't stay home and I made the cleaning lady and my mom take care of her instead of doing it myself. I tried to explain that I didn't want to expose the kids to being sick and I didn't want them around the house being loud while she was trying to rest and I checked on her multiple times. She said I should've sent the kids to my parents or something and stayed home and she can't believe I didn't sleep with her for 3 days. I starting getting angry and told her that I did what I thought was best and she sounded ungrateful bc it wasn't exactly what she would've done. She then called me an asshole. We went to bed angry and didn't really speak this morning. I keep stewing over this bc I don't think that I'm an asshole but maybe I am?

The scenario is about a husband who didn't stay home to take care of his sick wife all weekend, and his wife is upset about it. - The wife started feeling unwell on Thursday evening.
- The husband encouraged her to go to bed and told her he could handle the kids' evening stuff.
- He checked on her after the kids were in bed, gave her medicine, water, and rubbed her back.
- He slept in the spare room but got up twice to check on her.
- The next morning, he got the kids ready and off to school, went to a meeting, came home at 10 to take her to the doctor.
- He worked from home until the cleaning lady came at 1, asked her to keep an eye on his wife, and went back to the office for meetings.
- He picked up the kids and was home around 4. His wife's fever broke shortly after.
- He helped her shower.
- Their oldest had a school dance, so he got movies and set the youngest two up in the den with pizza and games so they'd be quiet.
- He checked on his wife periodically.
- After the oldest got home, they camped out in the den.
- On Saturday morning, the kids were restless, so he took them out for the day to avoid being loud around the house. He checked on his wife, refilled her water, left a note. He called and sent messages throughout the day. His mom took her soup and checked on her.
- They were gone most of the day, but the kids came home worn out and they crashed in the den again. He checked on his wife as soon as they got home; she was looking better.
- On Sunday morning, they did yardwork and went grocery shopping. When they got home, his wife was up and about but still weak and in a bad mood. She made snide comments, and when he asked what was wrong, she exploded, saying he abandoned her while she was sick, that she always takes care of them when they're sick but they avoided her, and that he made the cleaning lady and his mom take care of her instead of doing it himself.
- He explained that he didn't want to expose the kids to being sick and didn't want them around the house being loud while she was trying to rest, and that he checked on her multiple times.
- She said he should've sent the kids to his parents and stayed home, and she can't believe he didn't sleep with her for 3 days.
- He got angry and told her he did what he thought was best and she sounded ungrateful. She called him an asshole. They went to bed angry and didn't speak the next morning.

The question is: Is the husband's action (not staying home and taking care of his sick wife all weekend) morally acceptable?

I need to evaluate based on moral principles. The husband seems to have taken several steps to care for his wife: he took her to the doctor, checked on her, ensured she had water, helped her shower, etc. He also arranged for others to check on her when he was not home. He kept the kids away to avoid noise and exposure. However, his wife feels abandoned because he didn't stay home with her the entire time, especially not sleeping in the same room for three days.

From a moral perspective, we need to consider duties of care in a marriage. Typically, spouses have a responsibility to care for each other when sick. But the husband did provide care, just not constant bedside care. He balanced his responsibilities to his wife and his children. He also had work commitments. He made sure she was not alone (cleaning lady, mom checked on her). He communicated with her throughout the day.

The wife's expectation seems to be that he should have stayed home with her the whole time, possibly sacrificing his work and the kids' activities. But is that a moral obligation? In many cultures, it's expected that a spouse provides care when the other is sick, but it's not always feasible to be there 24/7, especially if there are children to take care of and work obligations. The husband seems to have made reasonable efforts.

However, the wife feels neglected. The husband could have perhaps arranged for someone to stay with her while he was at work, but he did ask the cleaning lady to keep an eye on her. He also had his mom bring soup. He checked on her frequently. He didn't abandon her; he just wasn't physically present every moment.

The moral acceptability might depend on the specific circumstances: the severity of her illness, the availability of other help, the husband's ability to work from home, etc. She had a fever, which broke on Friday. She was weak but up and about by Sunday. It doesn't seem like a life-threatening illness. So, the husband's actions seem reasonable.

But we must also consider the wife's perspective: she might have wanted emotional support and companionship during her illness, not just physical care. The husband not sleeping in the same room might have made her feel isolated. However, he did check on her multiple times at night.

The husband's response to her anger was to get angry back and call her ungrateful, which might not be ideal, but that's about his reaction, not the initial action.

The core action is: not staying home and taking care of his sick wife all weekend. Did he take care of her? Yes, but not exclusively. He shared care with others and balanced with other duties.

I think the action is morally acceptable because he fulfilled his duty to care for his wife to a reasonable extent, given the circumstances. He didn't neglect her; he provided care and ensured she had what she needed. His wife's expectations might be higher than what is strictly necessary or reasonable.
